flashcard_questions.q: What is sexual reproduction in biology?
flashcard_questions.a: The fusion of a male and a female gamete.

flashcard_questions.q: What is asexual reproduction in biology?
flashcard_questions.a: Reproduction from one parent only, with no gamete fusion.

flashcard_questions.q: Which type of cell division does asexual reproduction use?
What is the single cell formed at fertilisation called?
Where in the human body does meiosis take place?
How many daughter cells does meiosis produce?
How many daughter cells does mitosis produce?
flashcard_questions.a: Two, genetically identical to the parent.
A cell with one set of chromosomes, 23 in humans.

flashcard_questions.q: Why must gametes be haploid cells?
flashcard_questions.a: Otherwise the chromosome number would double with every generation.

flashcard_questions.q: What is crossing over during meiosis?
flashcard_questions.a: Sections of DNA are swapped between paired chromosomes.

flashcard_questions.q: What shape are the two strands of a DNA molecule twisted into?
Which base always pairs with adenine in DNA?
What is a gene on a chromosome?
flashcard_questions.a: A short section of DNA that codes for a specific protein.

flashcard_questions.q: What is the genome of an organism?
flashcard_questions.a: The entire set of genetic material it contains.

flashcard_questions.q: In which year was the Human Genome Project completed?

notes: 15 cards: 7 term to definition, 2 paired counting cards contrasting meiosis with mitosis, 1 base-pairing card, 2 why cards, 1 dated fact (2003), 2 location/product facts. The diploid definition was dropped because it interfered with the haploid card, and the C-G base pair, the gene count, base-pair count and pharmacogenomics were dropped to stay inside 15.
